ward_summary.measure_note: Bicyclist-involved crash COUNTS by Boston City Council District, 2021-01-01 onward (~5 years, matching DC and Chicago window length as a consistency choice). Source: City of Boston Vision Zero Crash Records (data.boston.gov). NOT exposure-adjusted -- no per-district ridership data available. Boston's VZ data has no e-bike-specific flag. As of 2026 Boston's public crash file no longer includes ANY injury-severity field (no more 'Fatal injury' vs 'Non-fatal injury' vs 'No injury') -- the 'fatal' count here is instead an APPROXIMATE match against Boston's separate Vision Zero Fatality Records file, joined by nearest timestamp (within 6h) and location (within ~1km) since the two files share no common id; this recovers most but not all known bike fatalities, so 'fatal' is a lower bound, and the 'injury' count below is really just 'not matched as fatal', not a confirmed injury. District assigned via point-in-polygon against official City Council District boundaries -- no district field in the crash records directly. 'near_bike_lane' means within ~30m of an OSM-mapped cycleway (infrastructure context, not a cause).

bikeshare_context.measure_note: Bluebikes monthly trip data (hubway-data S3 bucket -- Bluebikes was originally called Hubway). Same Lyft platform as Capital Bikeshare and Divvy; same rideable_type field distinguishing electric_bike from classic_bike per trip. Covers ONLY Bluebikes' own fleet -- says nothing about personally-owned e-bikes. Shown as citywide context, not blended into district crash counts.

ward_exposure.measure_note: NOT a true risk-per-rider rate -- same caveat as DC and Chicago. Numerator (crashes) includes ALL cyclists; denominator (Bluebikes trips) is Bluebikes' fleet only. Read as 'crash activity relative to Bluebikes activity', not 'risk per cyclist'.
